subject: Order Form: payee entity, invoice cutover & tax jurisdiction questions
messages:
From: Sophie Li <sophie@hydraai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom@hydraai.com>, Hydra AI Legal <legal@hydraai.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice payee & VAT - Hydra AI PO attached

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again — attaching our PO (HydraAI_PO_1234.pdf). A quick operational ask from our finance team before we sign the order form: can invoices be issued to our UK subsidiary, "Hydra AI UK Ltd", instead of our US HQ?

Reason: our treasury needs the invoice pulled to the UK entity to avoid cross-border VAT withholding. If Redwood requires the US entity for contracting reasons, we can accept a short transitional window, but finance will need:

- Confirmation of the billing/payee name and address that will appear on invoices
- Redwood's tax ID (W‑9 or equivalent) or confirmation of withholding responsibility
- Any required tax evidence we should provide (e.g., VAT registration) – attaching our UK VAT cert (HydraAI_tax_cert_UK.pdf)

Also, what are your standard net terms on order forms for enterprise buys? We typically operate net30 but can be flexible with approvals.

Appreciate a short note on the options + who from Redwood we should loop in for legal redlines.

Best,
Sophie Li
Finance Operations
Hydra AI

Attachments: HydraAI_PO_1234.pdf, HydraAI_tax_cert_UK.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>
To: Sophie Li <sophie@hydraai.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice payee & VAT - Hydra AI PO attached

Sophie — thanks for the PO and the VAT cert. Looping legal and billing to get aligned. Quick summary of viable approaches from our side:

1) Contract with Redwood Inc. (US) but route invoices to the Hydra AI UK Ltd payee via our entity-mapping (standard for customers with multi-entity setups). Requires invoice recipient field and PO to match.

2) Contract + invoice both issued to Redwood UK entity (we can accommodate if deal size & region support it) — this requires internal approvals and slightly different accounting flow (may affect timing).

3) Transitional approach: sign with Redwood US, issue first N invoices to US while we process entity change; provide one-time credit to offset any double-VAT exposure (if needed) — would need commercial approval.

Net terms: our default is Net30 for self-serve; enterprise order forms commonly go Net45 or Net60 depending on procurement. I'll propose Net45 as a baseline for this deal unless finance indicates otherwise.

Kimberly — can you advise on redlines we should expect if they want the contracting party to be their UK subsidiary vs. payee-only change? Also confirm what tax evidence we need on file and whether we can offer a short-term credit if we accept invoices to the Hydra UK payee before our entity switch is fully processed.

Action items:
- Kimberly: legal preference + redline checklist
- Karthik/Monica: confirm billing system support for entity-mapped invoicing and any timing impacts
- Sophie/Tom: confirm preferred payee name, address, VAT/GST ID to put on PO and invoice

Thanks — Vivek
Head of Commercials | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_OrderForm_v3.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.inference>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>
Cc: Sophie Li <sophie@hydraai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Invoice payee & VAT - Hydra AI PO attached

Vivek / team — forwarding my notes after a quick read of PO and the ask. Key points from legal that will affect the Order Form / MSA redlines:

- If Hydra requires the contracting counterparty to be "Hydra AI UK Ltd" (i.e., party on the MSA/Order Form), we need to:
  * Change the counterparty entity on the signature block and update the governing law clause (UK entities sometimes request English law) — expect 1–2 business days for a targeted redline + commercial signoff.

- If the request is payee-only (i.e., contract remains with Redwood US but invoices are addressed to Hydra AI UK Ltd), we can support via our entity-mapping flow. Requirements:
  * Signed order form indicating invoice recipient;
  * Hydra to provide VAT registration evidence (we have received the VAT cert, but need confirmation it covers the invoicing entity);
  * Affirmation of who bears withholding/tax liabilities (we recommend Hydra certifies no UK withholding applies to Redwood — if not, Hydra may need to withhold and remit).

- Credits / remediation: legal is OK with a one-time commercial credit to mitigate double VAT exposure, but we need this documented in an amendment to the Order Form (short addendum).

Risks / asks:
- If contracting moves to the UK entity and they request English law, that triggers additional legal review (data transfer and export controls checklist) and may impact timeline.
- We should avoid open-ended tax indemnities. Any indemnity must be scoped to identified tax amounts and timeboxed.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Sophie/Tom to confirm whether they want (A) contract-party change, or (B) payee-only invoice routing.
2) If (B), provide VAT reg number tied to the payee and preferred invoice address + PO number mapping.
3) Redwood to draft a one-page amendment if credit is agreed; legal will prepare redline if contracting party changes.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Thanks Kimberly — appreciate the clarity. To confirm Hydra's preference: we want option (B) — contract stays with Redwood US, invoices issued to Hydra AI UK Ltd (payee-only). We provided the VAT cert for the UK entity; attached is the signed PO referencing the UK payee.

A couple of operational clarifications so we can get to signature this week:

- Invoice header should read: Hydra AI UK Ltd | 12 Bridge Road, London, UK | VAT: GB123456789
- Redwood to confirm the payee field will appear on the invoice PDF and that the PO number will map to that payee in your accounting system
- If a temporary double-VAT exposure arises during cutover, we would request a one-time credit equal to the VAT amount billed twice (we can provide examples). We understand this needs to be documented as an amendment.
- Net terms: Net45 is acceptable. Can you confirm that on the order form?

If you can confirm these items and send the small amendment/one-pager for the credit, we can route back to procurement and sign. If helpful, happy to take a 20-minute call tomorrow morning to avoid back-and-forth.

Cheers,
Tom Nguyen
Head of Finance | Hydra AI
